sentences.text: The known specimen is a fairly complete skeleton of a subadult individual measuring 3.26 meters in total length.
Its skull was 23.7 centimeters long, featuring a snout angled at 15 degrees and a rectangular bony bar separating the eyes.
The vertebrae along the neck had high, triangular spines shaped like shark fins, while the three pectoral vertebrae possessed rectangular spines pointing slightly backward.
The forelimb bones were about 24 centimeters long and oval in cross-section, whereas the single available hindlimb bone measured 21.5 centimeters with one concave edge.
Soft tissue was apparently preserved within the fossil but was removed during the preparation process.
Sediment found in the belly area might have been stomach contents, possibly including swallowed stones and digested bones.
Laborers uncovered the holotype near Gronau in northwestern Germany in July 1910 using pickaxes, an event that shattered the pubic bone into 176 fragments.
This specimen, cataloged as GPMM A3.B4, is now held at the University of Münster and comes from the Isterberg Formation.
Earlier fragmentary remains found in Lower Saxony led Ernst Koken to describe two species of Plesiosaurus in 1887.
This animal likely hunted ray-finned fish such as Caturus, Lepidotes, Coelodus, Ionoscopus, and Ainia in the surface waters.
Fossils from this lake environment were presumably preserved after the animals sank to the oxygen-poor lake bottom.
The species Brancasaurus brancai was named by Theodor Wegner in 1914 to honor Wilhelm von Branca, though a 2010 study by Ketchum and Benson placed it in the family Leptocleididae.
While it was once thought to be a basal elasmosaurid, modern phylogenetic analyses since 2010 confirm its membership or close relationship to the Leptocleididae family.
Its fossils come from the Bückeberg Group, which likely formed in a large continental freshwater lake that later expanded and became brackish due to marine transgression.

A cervical vertebra from southern England shows a similar shape, suggesting the taxon might have existed outside Germany, while researchers also found that Gronausaurus is virtually indistinguishable from Brancasaurus.
